paper_identity.title: Shell structure of superheavy nuclei in self-consistent mean-field models

cross_mass_significance: Exposes the complete breakdown of magic number transferability from 208Pb to the superheavy island of stability: proves that massive Coulomb repulsion creates an interior central density depression that quenches the spin-orbit potential by 30-40%, leading to competing proton shell closures (Z=114 in RMF vs Z=120/126 in Skyrme/Gogny) with small shell gaps (1.5-2.0 MeV) that succumb to quadrupole softness rather than forming rigid spherical magic cores.
